title: Breaking Down the new NBA Nike ad
description: Breaking Down the new NBA Nike ad
transcript: Today, I'm going to be breaking down the new Nike ad celebrating the Knicks championship win. This is genius and this is why. Firstly, the timing. They dropped it the day after high production. Ads like this are usually not this reactive, but it really feeds into the moment and helps them own it. The music choice is incredible. It's a song about someone rejecting Miami or Hollywood to be by the Hudson. New Yorkers are proud of their city and it really plays into that. It's also the only thing you hear. The visuals show typical New York chaos, but the music drowns it out. They really want you to feel something. Next, product placement. Nike has sponsored the NBA for the past nine years. The two brands go hand in hand. Nike doesn't need to do a hard sell. They need to become the culture and the feeling of the moment. The real genius part is it was actually filmed at the real life celebrations. So no sets or actors, real people celebrating the real moment. They captured the feeling that high production cinema only can, but with raw and authentic fans. And finally, the tagline is genius. Never slept, always dream. New York is the city that never sleeps. The next of the team who never gave up their dreams of winning the cup for 54 years. And it's completely on brand with Nike slogan, impossible as nothing. 10 out of 10. Great job, Nike.
